extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants preparing ERC Starting, Consolidator or Advanced Grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting ERC Starting, Consolidator and Advanced Grant proposals, including what panels evaluate at Step 1 and Step 2, required proposal structure, eligibility windows, and common reasons for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence is the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellence is the sole evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of excellence at two levels: (1) Excellence of the Research Project and (2) Excellence of the Principal Investigator. Proposals are assessed only against excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground‑breaking nature of the research project
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground breaking nature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel guidance: Pay particular attention to the ground‑breaking nature of the research project – no incremental research. State‑of‑the‑art is not enough. Think big! In Step 1 the extended synopsis must present this clearly as evaluators are not necessarily all experts in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the potential of the project to make substantial advances beyond the state of the art; explain why the idea is important and what substantial gains are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific approach (methodology and feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Approach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the methodology, feasibility, work plan, selection of case studies and coherence of figures. Provide sufficient detail (Step 2) on methodology and the work plan; justify requested resources and show feasibility. Include alternative strategies to mitigate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual capacity of the Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual capacity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the PI's intellectual abilities as shown by CV, track record and evidence of independent thinking and leadership appropriate to the career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity of the Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the PI's creativity and originality in approaching research problems and proposing novel directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment of the Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the PI's commitment to the project (ability to manage a 5‑year project, time dedication, institutional arrangements) and whether the PI is best/only person to carry it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI track‑record & evidence of independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential for research independence; evidence of scientific maturity and track‑record
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For StG/CoG: at least one (StG) or several (CoG) publications without participation of PhD supervisor; promising early achievements (publications, invited talks, funding, patents, awards). For AdG: substantial track‑record of significant research achievements in last 10 years (extended for career breaks). Show organisation contributions, leadership, and support of early careers. Use the provided CV model and track record pages in Part B1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project scope appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope should be appropriate (not too narrow or too broad/unfocussed)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical reason for rejection: project scope too narrow or too broad/unfocussed. Ensure objectives and boundaries are clearly defined and ambitious but feasible within the project timeframe and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work plan detail and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Work plan must be detailed and clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical reason for rejection: work plan not detailed enough/unclear. In Step 2 provide a coherent, detailed work plan in Part B2 (15 pages) explaining tasks, timeline, milestones, team roles and justification of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management and contingency strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide alternative strategies to mitigate risk and justify risk
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of project risks, justify why the risk is worth taking given potential gains, and include contingency plans/alternative strategies in the methodology and work plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal structure compliance (Part A, B1, B2 and annexes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow required administrative and scientific proposal structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative forms (Part A) and call‑specific questions must be completed. Part B1 (submitted as pdf) is evaluated in Step 1 & 2 and includes extended synopsis, CV and track record; Part B2 (pdf) is evaluated in Step 2 only and contains the 15‑page scientific proposal (state‑of‑the‑art, objectives, methodology, resources). Include annexes (host institution commitment, PhD certificates, etc.). Follow the 'Guidelines and Recommendations' in the Information for Applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B1 requirements for Step 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B1 is read at Step 1 (extended synopsis and PI info) and must be concise and clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B1 components and page limits: extended synopsis (5 pages), CV (2 pages), Track‑record (2 pages). In Step 1 panel members (generalists) see only Part B1: prepare it to highlight ground‑breaking nature, concise presentation (evaluators not necessarily specialists), outline feasibility and show scientific independence in CV (model CV provided). Fill in Funding ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B2 requirements for Step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B2 is evaluated in Step 2 and must provide detailed scientific content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not just repeat the synopsis. Provide sufficient detail on methodology, work plan, selection of case studies, coherence of figures, justify requested resources, explain involvement of team members, and include alternative strategies to mitigate risk. Part B2 length: 15 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to page limits and formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow formatting rules and page limits; a submitted proposal can be revised until the call deadline by overwriting the previous version. Download and proof‑read before submitting. Use the templates and instruction documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility windows and allowable extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: PhD year windows for Starting and Consolidator Grants and permitted extensions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition StG: PhD at least 2 and up to 7 years before reference date (e.g. 1 Jan 2018). Condition CoG: PhD at least 7 and up to 12 years before reference date. Extensions possible for documented cases (maternity 18 months per child before/after PhD, paternity = actual time off, military service, medical specialty training, caring for seriously ill family members). No limit to total extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Targeted Panel and secondary panel flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant chooses targeted panel and may flag one secondary review panel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant chooses the panel which is responsible for evaluation. Switching between panels is not possible unless applicant made a clear mistake or different expertise is required. Cross‑panel evaluation by members of other panels is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑step evaluation process (remote assessment, panel meeting, interview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single submission but two‑step evaluation: remote assessment of Part B1 (Step 1) and full proposal assessment (Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEP 1: Remote assessment by panel members of section 1, Part B1 (synopsis and PI), followed by panel meeting. STEP 2: Remote assessment by panel members and reviewers of full proposals (B1+B2), panel meeting + interview (StG+CoG). Proposals with score A retained for Step 2; B & C rejected with resubmission consequences. Feedback and redress mechanisms exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scheme and consequences (A, B, C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring: 'A' fully meets excellence and recommended for funding; 'B' meets some but not all excellence criteria and will not be funded; 'C' not of sufficient quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score 'A': recommended for funding if funds available. Score 'B': not funded; if B awarded in Step 1, PI may not submit a proposal to any call in the following year (example: if B in Step 1, PI may not submit in 2018). Score 'C': not sufficient to pass to Step 2; PI may be subject to resubmission limitations (examples given: may not submit in next 1 or 2 years). Panels use scoring to create ranked lists; A may be within/outside panel budget; reserve lists may be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and panel responsibility for resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Requested resources must be reasonable and well justified; panels analyse budget in Step 2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget analysis carried out in Step 2 evaluation meeting. Panels ensure resources requested are reasonable and well justified. Budget cuts need to be justified per proposal; panels recommend a final maximum budget based on resources allocated/removed. Panels do not micro‑manage finances. Awards are made on a 'take‑it‑or‑leave‑it' basis; no negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external specialised reviewers in Step 2
rubrics_metrics.description: In Step 2 both Part B1 and B2 are sent to specialists (external referees)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2 involves specialised external referees worldwide; the proposal must therefore include sufficient technical detail for specialist review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution commitment and eligibility of HI
rubrics_metrics.description: Host Institution letter of support required; HI must be in EU or H2020 associated country
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get a letter of support from the Host Institution where the project will be carried out. Include commitment of the host institution as an annex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant self‑assessment checklist/questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions applicants should ask themselves about competitiveness and project merits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key questions: Am I internationally competitive at my career stage and discipline? Can I work independently and manage a 5‑year project with a substantial budget? Why is my project important? Does it go substantially beyond state of the art? Why am I the best/only person to carry it out? Is it timely? What's the risk and do I have a plan to manage it?

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reasons for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical reasons proposals are rejected for PI and project weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Principal Investigator: insufficient track record, insufficient (potential for) independence, insufficient experience in leading projects. For Proposed project: scope too narrow or too broad/unfocussed, incremental research, work plan not detailed enough/unclear, insufficient risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative compliance and use of help tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical submission advice and resources to use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register early, get familiar with the system and templates, start filling the forms, use help tools and call documents (Information for Applicants, Work Programme, FAQs), talk to National Contact Points and institutional grant offices, view step‑by‑step videos and check ERC funded projects, past panel members and statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for B1 components and B2
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific page limits for parts of the proposal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B1: extended synopsis 5 pages; Curriculum Vitae 2 pages; Track‑record 2 pages. Part B2 (scientific proposal): 15 pages. Ensure these limits are respected.
